overclaims: Section 4.2 establishes information-reporting requirements, including safety-test information, without a mandatory independent authorization process before release.
checks.note: The rationale's claim about Section 4.2 relies on the primary order text (govinfo). That text was read but is not one of the evidence items. The only outcome item is TIME (e1). It says the order requires safety-test disclosure and does not set out what follows if a model is reported as dangerous. The same article notes experts are divided on whether the government could act. So e1 does not by itself show that no authorization gate exists. The e1 explanation's line 'Reading section 4.2 confirms' is also unsupported in the payload. Fix by adding the order text as an evidence item or narrowing the rationale.

The excerpt is verbatim, and 'depends heavily' fairly renders 'depends a lot'. GAO e1 supports the point that implementation problems (90 days, incomplete DHS guidance) contributed to weak risk assessments. BIS e2 supports the documented reporting step. The rationale correctly says neither source shows how much effectiveness depended on wording, enforcement or mandatory status, which matches the agreed outcome of unresolved. e1's event_date of 2024-01 is the assessment deadline, and available_at is 2024-12-18. Both are stated consistently.
